mainEntity.name: Are surgical guides suitable for all implant cases?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most implant cases can benefit from surgical guides, though suitability depends on individual anatomy, bone quality, and treatment complexity. Some situations may require traditional placement techniques or additional procedures before guided surgery becomes viable. Clinical assessment determines the most appropriate approach for each patient.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to create a surgical guide?

acceptedAnswer.text: The process typically takes 1-2 weeks from initial scanning to guide fabrication. This includes time for digital planning, guide design, and manufacturing. Complex cases requiring extensive planning may take longer, whilst simpler single-implant guides can often be produced more quickly.

mainEntity.name: Is guided implant surgery more expensive than traditional placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Guided surgery often involves additional costs for scanning, planning software, and guide fabrication. However, the enhanced precision may reduce complications and revision procedures, potentially offering better value long-term. Treatment costs should be discussed during consultation, considering individual circumstances and treatment complexity.

mainEntity.name: Will I need multiple surgical guides for several implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single surgical guide can typically accommodate multiple implants in the same treatment area. The guide contains precisely positioned holes for each planned implant location. Separate guides may be needed if implants are being placed in different areas of the mouth or during separate treatment phases.

mainEntity.name: Can surgical guides be used with immediate implant placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, surgical guides can often be used for immediate implant placement following tooth extraction. The digital planning process accounts for both extraction and implant placement procedures. However, this depends on bone quality, extraction site healing potential, and other individual factors requiring clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the surgical guide doesn't fit properly during surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly fabricated guides should fit accurately based on pre-surgical scans. However, if fit issues arise, the procedure may be modified or converted to traditional placement techniques. This emphasises the importance of choosing experienced practitioners with appropriate backup planning protocols.
